result.topic_en: Euler sets up the general evolution of numbers of the form N = 40aa + 13bb. He splits it into two cases (μ = 10, ν = 4 and μ = 20, ν = 2) and tabulates the values S to be subtracted from aa, with their differences.
result.transcription:
— 28 —

num de factoribus imparibus est tenendum, notetur si $a$ sit numerus par et potestatem quamcunque ipsius binarii involvat, tum utrumque factorem $y+b=\mu p$ et $y-b=\nu q$ parem esse debere. Unde si ipsi $\mu$ valor par tribuatur, nihil impedit quo minus et $\nu$ par statuatur, id quod facile in exemplis oblatis observare licet. Ita cum numerus $520=8.5.13$ in tabula superiore numerorum idoneorum contineatur, secundum praecepta hic tradita in genere numeros $N=40aa+13bb$ evolvamus.

Evolutio generalis
numerorum contentorum in forma
$N=40aa+13bb.$

§. 46. Hic igitur erit $\alpha=40$ et $\beta=13$, atque hinc numeros $x$ et $y$ ex sequenti forma elicere licebit:
$40aa-13(yy-bb)=40xx$
ubi statim duos casus distingui conveniet, quibus est vel $\mu=10$ et $\nu=4$, vel $\mu=20$ et $\nu=2$, quia scilicet ambo factores debent esse pares.

Casus I.
quo $\mu=10$ et $\nu=4$.

§. 47. Hic igitur erit $y+b=10p$ et $y-b=4q$, hincque $b=5p-2q$. Fractioni ergo $\frac{5}{2}$ proxima erit $\frac{2}{1}$, unde statuamus $p=2s+b$ et $q=5s+2b$, quibus valoribus substitutis aequatio resolvenda erit
$aa-13(2s+b)(5s+2b)=xx.$
Posito igitur brevitatis gratia numerum a quadrato $aa$ subtrahendum, scil. $13(2s+b)(5s+2b)=S$, si loco $s$ suc-
cessi-

— 29 —

cessive scribamus numeros $0, \pm1, \pm2, \pm3$, etc. valores ipsius $S$ cum suis differentiis, quorum usum jam saepius explicavimus, ita se habebunt:

$s$ | $S$ | Diff.
$0$ | $26bb$ |
$\pm1$ | $13(2\pm b)(5\pm 2b)$ | $130\pm117bb$
$\pm2$ | $13(4\pm b)(10\pm 2b)$ | $390\pm117bb$
$\pm3$ | $13(6\pm b)(15\pm 2b)$ | $650\pm117bb$
$\pm4$ | $13(8\pm b)(20\pm 2b)$ | $910\pm117bb$
etc. | etc. | etc.

quae differentiae continuo crescunt augmento constanti 260; unde facile, quousque libuerit, continuabuntur; ubi autem probe notetur, subtractionem differentiarum fieri debere a numero $aa-26bb$.

Casus II.
quo $\mu=20$ et $\nu=2$.

§. 48. Hic igitur erit $y+b=20p$ et $y-b=2q$, unde, cum hinc fiat $b=10p-q$, sumto $p=s$ fiet $q=10s-b$, et aequatio resolvenda erit: $aa-13pq=xx$ sive $aa-13s(10s-b)=xx$. Posito igitur brev. gr. $13s(10s-b)=S$, valores ipsius $S$, prout $s$ fuerit vel $0$, vel $1$, vel $2$, vel $3$, erunt sequentes:

$s$ | $S$ | Diff.
$0$ | $0$ |
$\pm1$ | $13(10\pm b)$ | $130\pm13b$
$\pm2$ | $26(20\pm b)$ | $390\pm13b$
$\pm3$ | $39(30\pm b)$ | $650\pm13b$
$\pm4$ | $52(40\pm b)$ | $910\pm13b$
etc. | etc. | etc.

ubi

items.quote: notetur si $a$ sit numerus par et potestatem quamcunque ipsius binarii involvat, tum utrumque factorem $y+b=\mu p$ et $y-b=\nu q$ parem esse debere.
items.english: Note that if a is an even number and involves any power of two, then both factors y+b=μp and y−b=νq must be even.

items.quote: secundum praecepta hic tradita in genere numeros $N=40aa+13bb$ evolvamus.
items.english: Following the rules given here, let us evolve in general the numbers N = 40aa + 13bb.

items.quote: quae differentiae continuo crescunt augmento constanti 260
items.english: These differences increase continually by the constant increment 260.
